what_worked: Honest mean-vs-median callout on slide 3 and transparent acknowledgment of data missingness on slide 12.
fix_next: The deck reframes a class dataset as a fictional VC fund pitch, burying analytical insight under promotional spin—interrogate the data, don't sell it.
verdict: Polished LP pitch wrapper around real data, but insight stays shallow and promotional.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1/2: '$161.7M aggregate annualized run-rate' implies $13.47M MRR × 12 = $161.7M, but total 30-day revenue is $15.6M, not $13.47M; the MRR figure appears fabricated or uses an undisclosed filter. Slide 2: '$334.0M cumulative lifetime revenue' has no basis in the dataset (only 30-day revenue is available). Slide 3: Median stated as $400 but reference median across all 1000 companies should be closer to ~$282 if using MRR or the overall median is ambiguous—the $282 figure is stated in the footer of slide 2 but contradicted on slide 3. Slide 5: '26.5% generated by the single largest position' conflates anonymous-company revenue share (26.525%) with a single company; the 26.5% figure is the share from all 129 anonymous companies, not one company. Slide 12: '26% of the portfolio operates outside the US' contradicts slide 6 which says 74% are outside the US (the 26% figure is the US share of 258/1000 with country data, but 241 rows have missing country data, making the denominator wrong).

evidence.insight: Slide 3 mean-vs-median gap is the strongest analytical moment. Slide 5 concentration curve is relevant but the 26.5% claim is misattributed. Slide 9 valuation multiples add a useful lens. Overall, insights describe the data rather than interrogate it—no category-level median analysis, no provider-revenue efficiency comparison, no exploration of why 216 companies have zero revenue.
evidence.narrative: Clear LP-update arc: overview → health → composition → concentration → geography → stealth → infrastructure → valuation → highlights → methodology → risk → ask. Coherent sequence but the thesis ('diversification + breakouts') is asserted rather than tested. The narrative never challenges its own premise.
evidence.framing: The fictional VC fund framing is creative but obscures the analytical assignment. A cold reader would not know this is a student data-story exercise. Scope and limitations are partially addressed (slide 11-12) but missingness rates are understated and the 'coming soon' methodology slide is filler.
evidence.accuracy: MRR of $13.47M doesn't match total 30-day revenue of $15.596M. Cumulative lifetime revenue of $334M is invented. The 26.5% single-position claim misreads the anonymous cohort stat. The 74% outside-US figure ignores 241 missing country values (should be 74% of 759 known, not 1000). Category counts and company counts on slide 4 match reference data well. Provider pie chart percentages on slide 8 are approximately correct by company count.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark-navy/gold/teal palette throughout. Clean typography and hierarchy. Charts are simple and legible. Pie chart on slide 8 is acceptable. Bar charts on slides 4 and 6 are well-labeled. Cumulative curve on slide 5 is effective. Some slides are text-heavy KPI cards with no real chart (slides 2, 7, 9). The deck has visual sameness—every slide uses the same card-based layout.
evidence.ai_slop: Heavy consulting/pitch language throughout: 'high-velocity startups,' 'real-time visibility — by design,' 'punching well above its weight,' 'the outlier we underwrote for,' 'built to withstand the power law.' The fictional fund wrapper (Catalyst Ventures, Fund II raise, fake contact info) is elaborate set dressing that displaces analysis. Slide 11 'coming soon' methodology is pure filler.
